units.title: Strategy Pattern Overview
units.body:
# Strategy Pattern Overview

The Strategy Pattern enables you to define a family of algorithms, encapsulate each one as an independent collaborator, and make them interchangeable at runtime.

By separating the invariant workflow orchestration from volatile algorithmic or policy choices, your domain logic remains closed for modification yet open for extension.

## Architecture & Structure

```mermaid
graph TD
    Client[Client / Context] -->|delegates to| Strategy["<<interface>> Strategy"]
    Strategy --> ConcreteA[ConcreteStrategyA]
    Strategy --> ConcreteB[ConcreteStrategyB]
    Strategy --> ConcreteC[ConcreteStrategyC]
```

## Computational Complexity & Invariants

Using dedicated policy collaborators guarantees stable runtime characteristics:
$$\text{Cost}(n) = \mathcal{O}(1) \quad \text{vs} \quad \mathcal{O}(k \cdot n)$$
$$\sum_{i=1}^n \text{policy}_i(x) \le \text{Threshold}$$

![Strategy Pattern Collaboration](/media/strategy-pattern.svg)

In this module, you will:
1. **Identify stable roles**: isolate orchestration interfaces from concrete channel implementations.
2. **Handle changing policies**: model variable pricing and discount strategies as interchangeable policy collaborators.
3. **Connect policies to checkout**: inject policy collaborators into cart and checkout workflows.
4. **Integrate the complete workflow**: coordinate policy, state, and presentation into an end-to-end service.

units.title: Extensible notification routing
units.body: Design a notification router that can accept new delivery channels without rewriting the routing workflow. Keep the public API small and make collaborators replaceable.

hints.title: Start with the varying capability
hints.body: The router does not need to know concrete channel classes. It needs only something capable of sending a message.

hints.title: Store collaborators by key
hints.body: A map of channels keyed by channel name lets callers register new capabilities at runtime.

units.title: Changing Policies
units.body:
# Changing Policies

In real-world business domains, pricing, discounting, and promotional rules change frequently. Hardcoding these rules into core transactional workflows causes coupling and regression risks.

By applying the Strategy Pattern to policies:
- Each calculation rule is encapsulated behind a shared policy interface.
- New discounting mechanisms can be introduced without touching existing ordering or billing code.
- Different policies can be composed or selected dynamically based on user tier, seasonal campaigns, or cart attributes.

units.title: Strategy policies assessment
units.body: Check your understanding of stable roles, replaceable policies, and deterministic strategy selection before continuing to the implementation exercises.

quiz.title: Strategy policies assessment
quiz.description: A deterministic assessment covering the strategy pattern and changing policy collaborators.

questions.prompt: Answer the required questions. Optional questions add practice but do not prevent submission.
What should remain stable when a discount policy changes?

options.label: Every concrete discount rule in the workflow

questions.explanation: The strategy boundary protects the stable workflow while policy implementations can change.

questions.prompt: Select the properties of a useful strategy collaborator.

options.label: It can be replaced without rewriting orchestration
It requires callers to know private implementation state

questions.explanation: Shared contracts and replaceability are the useful properties; callers should not depend on private state.

questions.prompt: A 10% discount on 100 leaves what subtotal?
questions.explanation: The unchanged workflow delegates the calculation to the selected policy.
Tolerance answers are useful when a deterministic result has an accepted numerical approximation.

questions.prompt: Enter a valid percentage from 0 through 100.
questions.explanation: Range answers express a deterministic inclusive interval.

questions.prompt: A new concrete strategy should require changing the stable checkout orchestration.
questions.explanation: The strategy boundary is intended to keep the stable orchestration closed for modification.

questions.prompt: What interface name describes the shared policy contract in this course?
questions.explanation: Short text answers are normalized and matched against the deterministic accepted values.

units.title: Identify variable discount policies
units.body: Model variable discount policies as replaceable strategy collaborators. Implement a percentage discount and flat discount that conform to the policy interface.

hints.title: Define the policy contract
hints.body: Both flat and percentage discounts should implement an `apply(amount: number): number` method. Apply this hint to see both implementation files updated at once.

units.title: Connect policy to checkout
units.body: Connect the discount policy collaborator to the checkout pricing workflow so discounts apply cleanly to cart subtotals.

hints.title: Inject the policy
hints.body: Pass the discount policy into the checkout calculator rather than hardcoding discount rules.

units.title: Parking allocation workflow
units.body: Model a small parking allocation workflow that keeps allocation policy separate from ticket persistence. The stress test should be able to replace either collaborator.

hints.title: Keep policy and persistence separate
hints.body: The service coordinates a workflow. Allocation policy and ticket storage should be supplied collaborators.
